Hi Elena / Vertic procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put the proposed billing approach on paper so your finance team can validate revenue recognition and cash-flow timing. High level: Vertic is looking at a 24‑month prepay commitment with a stepped ramp in usage in the first six months; you asked for an approach that minimizes Year 1 cash impact while preserving a term discount.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Contract term: 24 months (multi‑year prepay, 2-year)
- Total prepay: $3,000,000 (list price before discount)
- Term discount applied: 18% on gross committed amount, net committed = $2,460,000
- Billing split proposal: split invoices across fiscal years to help Vertic’s FY24/FY25 budget cadence (options below)
- Ramp crediting: provide monthly ramp credits during the first 6 months while usage ramps to committed baseline, with a one‑time true‑up at month 6.

Options for invoice phasing to consider (we can pick one with your finance):
A) Fiscal-slice billing — Invoice 70% upfront in FY24, 30% in FY25 (single invoice each year).
B) Staggered quarterly invoices — Four invoices: two in FY24 (50%/20%), two in FY25 (20%/10%).
C) Full upfront with seller-side holdback — Redwood invoices 100% but holds 20% in escrow and issues monthly credits as usage ramps.

We included an attached term sheet with numbers and a short revrec guidance spreadsheet that maps each billing option to typical ASC 606 treatment and suggested amortization schedule. Could you loop in anyone from accounting who will review ASC 606 implications?

Next steps: if you confirm which billing option you prefer, I’ll coordinate with our finance team (Ben and Aditya copied) to produce a final invoice schedule and a DocuSign packet.

Laura / team / Elena —

Thanks for the context. I pulled together the finance view and a recommended operational approach that balances Vertic's FY24 cash preference and ASC 606 compliance. Summary recommendation: go with Option A (Fiscal slice 70/30) with invoice netting for ramp credits and a defined amortization schedule in the SOW. Details below.

1) ASC 606 treatment
- Revenue recognition should follow transfer of services over time. For a prepaid multi‑year agreement where performance obligations are satisfied evenly, we recommend straight‑line amortization over the 24‑month service period.
- The 70/30 cash timing does not by itself change the revenue pattern; the contract must clearly state the timing of performance to support straight‑line revrec. We'll add explicit language that service is provided evenly over the period and that the prepayment is deferred and recognized monthly.

2) Invoice netting for ramp credits
- We can structure ramp credits as invoice netting: Redwood will calculate monthly ramp credits based on the agreed baseline and include them as negative line items on each invoice for months 1–6. That avoids separate credit memos.
- Holdback approach (alternative): Redwood could hold 15% of Year 1 and release it monthly as credits; that adds some administrative work on our side but may be preferable if Vertic wants a single large upfront payment with a built‑in performance modifier.

3) Billing phasing recommendation (numbers aligned to the term sheet):
- Total net committed: $2,460,000 (after 18% term discount).
- Invoice 1 (FY24): $1,722,000 (70% of net committed) — net of Month 1–6 ramp credits applied as negative line items.
- Invoice 2 (FY25 Q1): $738,000 (30% balance).
- Monthly ramp credits: calculated as the difference between committed monthly baseline and actual usage, applied monthly for months 1–6; final true‑up at month 6 reconciles any residual credit or shortfall.

4) Tax / jurisdiction notes
- Tax jurisdiction depends on billing address and where the service is deemed delivered. We recommend Vertic provide the billing tax jurisdiction on the PO and we will mirror that on the invoice. For material state tax questions, we'll coordinate with Vertic's tax advisor and our tax counsel.

5) Contract language and SOW items
- Add 1–2 sentences in the SOW: (a) service delivered evenly over the term; (b) prepayment accounted as deferred revenue and recognized monthly; (c) ramp credits applied as invoice netting; (d) true‑up mechanics at month 6.
- Ben to prepare a short billing schedule annex that can be appended to the term sheet.

Attachments: revrec_guidance.xlsx (explains amortization schedules for Options A/B/C). I also uploaded a draft DocuSign envelope with the term sheet and billing annex to our DocuSign template library: https://docusign.com/template/reds-vertic-term-sheet

Next steps:
- Laura: confirm the 70/30 path with Elena and request PO + billing address (tax jurisdiction).
- If Vertic confirms, Ben will finalize the billing annex and send for signature. Monica will own the operational ramp checklist and month‑6 true‑up.
